steps.label: Games and Simulations
steps.content:
Games and Simulations

Computer programs that you play are not all the same kind of thing. Two important words for today are game and simulation.

  • Game: lets you explore an imaginary world and complete challenges, mostly for fun. Mario Kart and Pac-Man are games, the tracks and mazes are not real places.
  • Simulation: copies a real-life situation as closely as it can. A flight simulator copies flying a real plane. A virtual pet copies looking after a real animal.
  • The question to ask is: is this inventing a make-believe challenge, or is it trying to copy something real?

Today's vocabulary

  • Control: a way of directing what happens in a game or simulation.
  • Input: information you give to a computer, for example pressing a button.
  • Output: information the computer gives back to you, for example a sound or a picture on the screen.
  • Simulation: a program that copies something from real life.

steps.label: Check Your Understanding
steps.content:
Check Your Understanding

Questions to ask around the room:

  • What is the difference between a game and a simulation?
  • What is an input? Give an example from today's timeline.
  • What is an output? Give an example.
  • Which input device let players use their whole body to control a game?
  • Why do you think consoles kept changing how players control games?

steps.label: Design a Futuristic Controller
steps.content:
Design a Futuristic Controller

The timeline goes from turning dials in 1972 to using your whole body in 2010. What comes next?

Your task

  • Design a controller for a games console that does not exist yet.
  • How would the player interact with it? Think about what they press, touch, wear, or move.
  • What would the controller actually do? What kind of game would it be perfect for?
  • Use the Pen and Text tools to draw and label your design.

Open Controller Designer to draw your idea, then use Save as PNG to keep a copy.

Extra challenge

Pick one input device from today's timeline, for example the Wii's wireless controller. Write about how you think it actually works. When you move it through the air, how do you think that information gets from the controller to the console?
